newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to off.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to off.

text.p: Early calls ranged from 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 lower for CME live cattle futures while feeder cattle were mostly called steady to 0.100 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Further bull spreading action is likely in live cattle futures based on indications for Friday's monthly USDA Cattle on Feed report. The report is expected to show continued tight fed cattle supplies nearby and large placements onto feedlots which will lead to larger fed supplies later, analysts said.
Cash ideas were also mixed with some analysts continuing to look for higher fed cattle prices on the tight supplies.

However, others cited an easier tone to the choice cash beef market and reluctance by packers to pay more than $72 per cwt for live supplies. The market also looks technically weak after the reversal on Monday, they added.

Early projections on Friday's report for on-feed cattle supplies as of September 1 in the seven key states ranged from 88.2 to 92 percent of a year ago, with the number of cattle placed in feedlots seen at 106.6 to 119 percent and marketings at 92 to 98 percent of a year ago.

Feeder cattle were expected to again be influenced by the back months of live cattle which have been under pressure from the projections for larger supplies next year. However, lower corn futures indications could provide support, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.01 at $64.09 per cwt, its highest level since December 27.
